title: objectql(validation): an unevaluable severity:'warning' rule logs "write rejected: … fails closed" twice while the write is accepted 201 and persists
body:
Filing gate: ① a product defect with a named location and a live reproduction (an operator-facing log line that states the opposite of what the server did).
Reader: the `packages/objectql` validation lane (`src/validation/rule-validator.ts`), next PR touching the rule-validator advisory branch.
Dedupe (open AND closed): "validation rule warning severity unevaluable logs write rejected but write persists" → 22 hits, none on this (nearest: #22726, warning hits not surfaced to the client — closed, different; #13889, warning-rule log volume on machine paths — closed, different; #24720, a `parent`-reading rule refused as unevaluable — open, error severity, different).
reach: public HTTP entry, measured twice — `POST /api/v1/data/OBJECT` on a stock showcase boot with a runtime-authored object answers 201 while the server log says the write was rejected.
Path: records-forms.validation-rule-type-matrix
QA-source: #24779 · records-forms.validation-rule-type-matrix · negative[1] (the clause passed — the warning rule does not block; the defect is the log beside it)
Checklist item priority: P1
type: Bug

## What happens

`rule-validator.ts` states the contract in its header: "`severity` still governs blocking: an unevaluable `warning`/`info` rule is logged, never thrown — advisory rules stay advisory." The write path does exactly that: the write answers 201 and the row persists. But the log lines it prints for that rule say the opposite:

```
WARN Validation rule 'qa_unevaluable_warn' predicate failed to evaluate (…) — write rejected: a rule that cannot be evaluated fails closed, it is never skipped
WARN Validation rule 'qa_unevaluable_warn' (warning): Validation rule 'qa_unevaluable_warn' could not be evaluated (…) — write rejected.
```

The first is the predicate evaluator's fail-closed sentence (~L4517; the `when`-predicate twin ~L4699 carries the same words), emitted before severity is consulted; the second is the advisory branch's per-write `warn`, which embeds the unevaluable violation's own message, also ending "write rejected". An operator reading the log for a disputed write is told it was refused when it was stored — twice.

## Reproduction (stock showcase, `objectstack dev --seed-admin`, framework `580fd4ed`)

1. Admin cookie session.
2. `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_vr_probe` with `{"name":"qa_vr_probe","label":"QA","sharingModel":"public_read_write","fields":{"title":{"type":"text"}},"validations":[{"type":"script","name":"qa_unevaluable_warn","severity":"warning","message":"x","condition":"int(record.title) > 1"}]}` → 200.
3. `POST /api/v1/data/qa_vr_probe` `{"title":"abc"}` → **201**, row persisted (correct).
4. Server log: the two lines above, both saying "write rejected".

Expected: a log line that says the advisory rule could not be evaluated and the write proceeded (advisory). Actual: "write rejected … fails closed", twice. Control: the same rule at `severity:"error"` → 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` naming the rule — there the sentence is true.

## Fix direction

Decide the verb after severity: the fail-closed sentence belongs to the error-severity path only; the advisory path should say the rule was skipped as advisory (one line, not two). Pin the log text for both severities.

Full evidence chain: run record #24779 (records-forms.validation-rule-type-matrix block in the runner A evidence comment).
